changelog: When to Segment: Added a concise list of disambiguating follow-ups (main verb/voice, noun heads, postnominal locatives, negation/polarity markers, post‑verbal obliques, pronoun antecedents, short temporal/prepositional complements, multiword adjectival compounds, coordinated noun-number contexts) that should usually be held for disambiguation; clarified these are candidacy concerns that affect ranking, not hard forbiddances.

Priority Rules: Incorporated those same follow-ups as explicit demotion signals: any candidate that ends immediately before them should be ranked lower (not removed). Also stated that multiword adjectival compounds must stay with their head where possible, and reiterated the minimum-tag fallback for conservative low-confidence placements.

Decision Procedure: Made the two-step flow explicit about demotion (not prohibition): mark generously, then lower rank for candidates that end immediately before listed disambiguating triggers; if minimum boundaries are not met, add conservative low-confidence candidates at safe punctuation/conjunctions and rank them last.
